entries.claim: Hallucination — fluent, syntactically correct but factually inaccurate output — is a documented field-wide failure mode of the LLMs underlying all AI writing tools (2025 comprehensive survey).
entries.quote: Hallucination refers to the generation of content by an LLM that is fluent and syntactically correct but factually inaccurate or unsupported by external evidence.
entries.platform: arXiv (survey; Alansari & Luqman, 'Large Language Models Hallucination: A Comprehensive Survey')
entries.label: research-finding

coding.tool: LLMs (field-wide, underlying all AI writing tools)
coding.aspect: hallucination / factual accuracy of generated text (failure-mode definition)

entries.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed study of ~3 million user reviews of 90 AI mobile apps (1,000 manually annotated; 350 confirmed hallucination reports) found factual incorrectness the most frequently user-reported hallucination type, at 38% of confirmed instances — defined sample, not a population rate.
entries.quote: Factual Incorrectness (H1) emerged as the most frequently reported type, accounting for 38% of instances
entries.platform: Scientific Reports (peer-reviewed; '“My AI is Lying to Me”: User-reported LLM hallucinations in AI mobile apps reviews')
entries.label: research-finding

coding.tool: AI mobile apps (LLM-based, field-wide; 90-app review corpus)
coding.aspect: user-reported hallucination — factual incorrectness most frequent type (38% of 350 confirmed instances)

entries.claim: In a 2024 peer-reviewed test (Croatian Medical Journal), 65% of references ChatGPT produced for medical case reports were non-existent and 87% of the valid ones were over 10 years old — dated GPT-3.5/4-era evidence; models have changed since, and the page must say so.
entries.quote: Examination of the references produced by ChatGPT showed that 65% were non-existent, and that 87% of the valid references were older than 10 years.
entries.label: research-finding

coding.aspect: reference/citation fabrication in medical case reports (65% non-existent; dated GPT-3.5/4-era)

entries.claim: One long-term independent reviewer (Jon Dykstra, affiliate-disclosed, months of hands-on use, updated 2026-04-08) describes Koala AI one-shot drafts as well-structured — intro answers the query, relevant additions, auto-generated table — a single positive anecdote, not a population claim.
entries.quote: It creates a compelling introduction and answers the query quickly. But then it adds relevant information and added the benefits of consuming watermelon seeds. It even added a table, all by itself.
entries.label: independent-test

coding.aspect: one-shot draft quality and structure (intro, relevant additions, auto table)

entries.claim: An independent 10+ article test of Koala AI (Victoria Kurichenko, affiliate-disclosed, updated 2026-01-03) reports the tool consistently delivers articles shorter than the requested length setting.
entries.quote: Even if you choose to write the longest article with 10–12 paragraphs and 2,350–2,940 words, Koala AI Writer will anyway create a shorter article
entries.platform: behindrankings.com (independent blog, disclosed methodology: 10+ generated articles; affiliate-disclosed)
entries.label: independent-test

coding.aspect: output length vs requested length setting (consistently shorter)

entries.claim: The same tester reports Koala AI output on specialist topics (SEO) was too shallow for client delivery — single-tester anecdote.
entries.quote: Whenever I ask KoalaWriter to generate an article about SEO, I get shallow answers. I can't deliver this content to my clients.
entries.label: independent-test

coding.aspect: content depth on specialist topics (SEO) — too shallow for client delivery

entries.claim: A disclosed-methodology three-way test (60+ days, 400+ content pieces on live client work; affiliate-disclosed; pseudonymous author 'NTH Editor'; dated only to 2025) rated Jasper's long-form drafts highest of Jasper/Writesonic/Copy.ai — one test, coding flagged ambiguous.
entries.quote: Jasper consistently produced the highest-quality long-form content of the three tools
entries.platform: neuraltoolhub.com (independent test with disclosed methodology; affiliate-disclosed; author pseudonymous)
entries.label: independent-test

coding.aspect: long-form content quality vs Writesonic/Copy.ai (single three-way test; pseudonymous author, year-only date)

entries.claim: The same three-way test rated Writesonic best of the three for short-form social/ad copy — one test, coding flagged ambiguous (same caveats as EV-07).
entries.quote: For social media and ad copy, Writesonic was arguably the best of the three, consistently producing punchy, conversion-oriented short copy with strong hook variety.
entries.platform: neuraltoolhub.com (independent test with disclosed methodology; affiliate-disclosed; author pseudonymous)
entries.label: independent-test

coding.aspect: short-form social/ad copy quality vs Jasper/Copy.ai (same single test, same caveats)
